environment: Humpback whale numbers peak off the Queensland coast as the annual southern migration passes through Hervey Bay and the Gold Coast
Reef monitoring teams report encouraging signs of coral recovery on parts of the Great Barrier Reef ahead of this year's spring spawning
science: Australian researchers edge closer to cheaper, more efficient solar panel recycling, turning old panels into new energy infrastructure
sports: Queensland clubs gear up for a big September as the NRL and AFL finals series hits full swing
stories.overview: Spring bursts into life across South East Queensland as whales, wildflowers and warmer days signal the season's turn

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: Morning legends, welcome back to ParkSyde Bright Side, it's Monday the fourteenth of September and there is genuinely good stuff happening out there. I'm Alex Mercer, joined as always by the far too chirpy Jamie. Chirpy and proud of it, Alex. Spring has properly sprung and honestly the whole show today just feels like a big exhale after winter, we've got whales, we've got footy finals, we've got science nerds doing good things with old solar panels. Love a good solar panel yarn. Stick around, we've got the environment desk, science, footy finals fever and Sam's going to sort out whether you need the brolly or the boardies this week.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: Right, environment desk, and it is peak whale season out on the water. Humpbacks are cruising south past Hervey Bay and right down through the Gold Coast, and whale watching boats are absolutely chocka with people hoping for a breach. Nothing beats a good breach, ay, big fella just launching himself out of the drink for no reason other than he can. Meanwhile out on the reef, monitoring crews reckon they're seeing decent signs of coral bouncing back in spots, right on cue for spring spawning. That spawning event is one of the wildest things in nature, the whole reef basically goes off like fireworks under the water once a year. Fingers crossed for a big one this season, our reef deserves a win.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Science corner now, and this one's for anyone with an old solar panel gathering dust in the shed. Aussie researchers are getting properly good at recycling solar panels, pulling the silicon and metals back out instead of them ending up in landfill. It's such a simple idea done properly, we've been so focused on putting panels up that nobody really planned for what happens when they wear out. Turning old panels into new ones is exactly the kind of boring, brilliant science that actually matters. Boring and brilliant, that's basically the ParkSyde motto. Good on the boffins, keep at it.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, g'day everyone, Sam here with your South East Queensland outlook. We're firmly in spring mode now, expect mostly sunny days across Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast with top temps sitting in the mid to high twenties. Afternoon sea breezes will keep the coast comfortable, though it might get a touch sticky inland by midweek as spring humidity starts creeping back in. Keep an eye out for the odd afternoon storm cell building over the Range later in the week, nothing major yet, just the season warming up its arm. Back to you two.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Sports desk, and September means one thing in this state, finals footy. NRL and AFL finals are both in full swing and Queensland fans have got plenty to shout about, or scream at the telly about, depending how your team's travelling. There's nothing quite like finals atmosphere, even the servo feels tense on game day. Whatever happens, it's shaping up as a cracking few weekends of footy right through to the big dance. Get around your team, wear the jersey, embarrass yourself at the pub, it's all part of the tradition.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: And that's your ParkSyde Bright Side wrap for Monday. Whales offshore, coral coming good, solar panels getting a second life and finals footy cranking up, not a bad Monday at all. Honestly one of my favourite shows in a while, there's something about spring that just makes everything feel a bit more hopeful. Get outside today if you can, the weather's on your side. Big thanks to Sam for keeping us dry, or at least warned. We'll be back tomorrow with more good news from around Queensland and beyond. Until then, look after each other, and maybe go check out a whale if you get the chance. Catch you tomorrow, Queensland. This has been ParkSyde Bright Side.
